introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Holy Trinity. God passes before Moses and proclaims his name: the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and rich in kindness. Jesus tells Nicodemus that God so loved the world that he gave his only Son. Paul ends his letter with the blessing of the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Let us worship the one God who is love.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God so loved the world that he gave his only Son. Let us pray to the Father, through the Son, in the Holy Spirit.
intentions: For the Church: that she may reflect the communion of love of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families and communities: that they may live in peace and the God of love may be with them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel judged or condemned: that they may know that God sent his Son to save, not to condemn. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who do not know God: that they may discover his mercy and kindness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that every Sign of the Cross we make may be an act of faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you sent your Son and your Spirit to reveal your love. May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, your love, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with us always. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: So loved the world
reflection.body:
The mystery of the Trinity can seem far beyond us. Today's readings bring it close, by showing us who God is: love.

In the first reading, Moses climbs Mount Sinai, and God passes before him and proclaims his own name: "The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth." This is how God describes himself. Moses bows down and prays for a stubborn people: "pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance."

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks to Nicodemus and reveals the depth of that love: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life." The Father gives the Son. The Son gives himself. And God's purpose is salvation, not condemnation: "For God didn't send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him."

Paul ends his second letter to the Corinthians with a blessing that the Church has used ever since. Before it, he gives them simple advice: "Finally, brothers, rejoice! Be perfected. Be comforted. Be of the same mind. Live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you." Then he blesses them in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.

The Trinity tells us that God is not alone. From all eternity, God is a communion of love between Father, Son and Spirit. We were made in his image, for communion.

This week, make the Sign of the Cross slowly and thoughtfully each morning. And let your relationships reflect God's love: be patient, slow to anger and rich in kindness, as he is.
